title: Explain how a jet engine works

scenes.title: Jet Engine: Thrust by Reaction
scenes.narration: A jet engine creates forward motion, or thrust, by expelling a high-velocity jet of gas backward. This is a direct application of Newton's Third Law, pushing an aircraft forward at incredible speeds.

scenes.title: The Four Stages of Thrust
scenes.narration: A jet engine operates in a continuous cycle: intake, compression, combustion, and exhaust. This process is like a powerful, continuous explosion pushing the aircraft forward.

scenes.title: Key Components: Air to Power
scenes.narration: The fan draws air in, the compressor squeezes it, the combustor ignites fuel, and the turbine extracts energy to power the compressor, all before hot gases exit the nozzle.

scenes.title: Turbofan: Modern Aircraft Power
scenes.narration: Modern airliners use turbofan engines, where a large fan bypasses most air around the core. This design is significantly more fuel-efficient and quieter, generating up to 100,000 pounds of thrust.

scenes.title: Enabling Global Connectivity
scenes.narration: Jet engines have revolutionized travel, enabling rapid global connectivity and powering everything from commercial airliners to military jets. Their continuous evolution focuses on greater efficiency and reduced emissions.
